_comment: Per-page trailer/embed editorial for a small set of high-visibility YouTube pages. uploadDate values are YouTube watch-page publishDate strings converted to ISO dates, read on 2026-08-20. Do not copy lastChecked into uploadDate. Duration is omitted because it was not on the watch page in a verifiable form. contentUrl is omitted because BRYME does not host the files.

sports.name: PREMIER LEAGUE 2026/27 🔥 | THE WAIT IS OVER | OFFICIAL TRAILER ⚽🔥
sports.description: A YouTube video about the 2026/27 Premier League season, published by Azar_kattumulla on 11 August 2026. It is not a Premier League Productions upload.
sports.figcaption: A third-party YouTube season clip from the channel Azar_kattumulla — not a Premier League Productions video.
context: The player on this hub is a YouTube embed. The uploader is Azar_kattumulla. YouTube showed the clip as premiered on 11 August 2026. BRYME does not host the file, did not edit it, and does not run that channel. The uploader’s packaging uses the word official; the channel is not the Premier League’s own YouTube account, so do not read this as a league announcement.

It is here because this page is the front door to BRYME’s 2026/27 football desk — fixtures, match pages, and transfer trackers. A season-themed clip lets you stay on the hub instead of bouncing out for a video. It is not a source for kick-off times, tables, injuries, or signings. When BRYME publishes those, they come from club or league pages and are labelled.

If the player fails, open the same video on YouTube. Ads, comments, and whether the upload stays public are YouTube’s problem, not BRYME’s. Nothing in the montage should be treated as a BRYME prediction.

The 2026/27 Premier League season is scheduled to start on Friday 21 August 2026 with Arsenal against Coventry City, from the league calendar used on BRYME’s football pages. Use the fixture links on this hub for dates. A YouTube clip is not the fixture list.

squid-game.name: Squid Game | Official Trailer | Netflix
squid-game.description: Netflix’s YouTube trailer for Squid Game, published 1 September 2021.
squid-game.figcaption: Netflix’s own YouTube trailer for the series. It loads only when you press play; BRYME does not host the file.
context: The player is Netflix’s YouTube trailer for this series, published on the Netflix channel on 1 September 2021. BRYME does not host or re-encode it. The still you see before play is YouTube’s public preview image for that video. Sound does not start until you press play.

A trailer is a marketing cut. It is not a recap, not a season index, and not BRYME’s review. It sits on this title page so you can see how the platform introduced the show before you read the notes written here. This page lists a South Korean series from 2021, in Korean, with Hwang Dong-hyeok as director and Lee Jung-jae, Lee Byung-hun and Wi Ha-joon in the billed cast. BRYME files it under survival, thriller and drama.

If the embed is blocked where you are, use the YouTube link under the frame. Full-episode availability is a licensing question that changes by country. That belongs in Where to watch legally on this page, not in the trailer. BRYME is not Netflix and does not claim the series is on any service unless a licensed link is listed.

alice-in-borderland.name: Alice in Borderland | Official Trailer | Netflix
alice-in-borderland.description: Netflix’s YouTube trailer for Alice in Borderland, published 28 October 2020.
alice-in-borderland.figcaption: Netflix’s YouTube trailer for the Japanese series, embedded so you can see the studio pitch before the synopsis.
context: This embed is Netflix’s YouTube trailer for the series, published on 28 October 2020 on the Netflix channel. BRYME does not host the video. The player uses YouTube’s privacy-enhanced domain and does not autoplay.

The clip is the platform’s marketing, not a walkthrough of the games and not a BRYME explainer. It is on this page because the title is one of the five homepage heroes, and this is the catalogue page those slides point to. BRYME lists a Japanese series from 2020, in Japanese, directed by Shinsuke Sato, with Kento Yamazaki, Tao Tsuchiya, Nijirō Murakami, Ayaka Miyoshi, Aya Asahina and Dori Sakurada in the billed cast. The genres on this page are survival, thriller and sci-fi.

The synopsis on this page is BRYME’s own catalogue text. Do not treat the trailer as a plot guarantee or as evidence of how many seasons exist. If the player fails, use the YouTube fallback. For legal full-episode options, use Where to watch legally — BRYME does not stream the show.

into-the-badlands.name: Official Comic Con Trailer: Into the Badlands: World Premiere
into-the-badlands.description: AMC’s Comic-Con premiere trailer for Into the Badlands, published on the amc+ YouTube channel on 11 July 2015.
into-the-badlands.figcaption: AMC’s Comic-Con premiere trailer from the amc+ YouTube channel — an early look, not a later-season recap.
context: The video on this page is the Comic-Con premiere trailer uploaded to the amc+ YouTube channel on 11 July 2015. That is the title YouTube still shows. It is an early marketing clip for the series, not a compilation of later seasons and not a BRYME-made recap. BRYME does not host the file.

It belongs here because this is the title page for a series BRYME also uses on the homepage carousel. The catalogue lists a United States series from 2015, in English, with Daniel Wu, Orla Brady, Sarah Bolger, Aramis Knight, Emily Beecham and Oliver Stark in the billed cast. Directors recorded on this page include Guy Ferland, David Dobkin, Toa Fraser, Stephen Fung and Paco Cabezas. BRYME files it as action, adventure and fantasy.

Press play only if you want that 2015 Comic-Con cut. It will not tell you how many seasons exist or where to stream them today. For that, use the details and Where to watch legally sections on this page. If YouTube blocks the embed, follow the fallback link under the frame.

solo-leveling.name: Solo Leveling | OFFICIAL TRAILER
solo-leveling.description: Crunchyroll’s YouTube trailer for Solo Leveling, published 3 July 2022.
solo-leveling.figcaption: Crunchyroll’s YouTube trailer for the anime. Published in 2022; BRYME lists the TV series year as 2024.
context: The embed is Crunchyroll’s YouTube trailer, published on 3 July 2022. BRYME does not host it. The thumbnail is YouTube’s public preview for that video ID. Playback starts only when you press play.

Note the dates. YouTube’s publish date for this clip is 2022. BRYME’s catalogue year for the TV series is 2024. That is not a contradiction we paper over: an early trailer can exist before the broadcast year on the title page. This page does not claim which cour or season the clip covers beyond what the uploader put on YouTube.

BRYME lists this as Japanese-language anime in action, fantasy and adventure, based on Chugong’s Korean web novel and manhwa, following Sung Jinwoo. Director and billed cast are not filled on this page, so they are not invented here either. The trailer is Crunchyroll’s marketing, not a substitute for those credits.
If you arrived from the homepage hero, this is the same verified clip. For legal streaming, use Where to watch legally. BRYME is not Crunchyroll.

nosferatu.name: NOSFERATU - Official Trailer [HD] - Only In Theaters December 25
nosferatu.description: Focus Features’ YouTube trailer for Nosferatu (2024), published 30 September 2024.
nosferatu.figcaption: Focus Features’ theatrical trailer for Robert Eggers’s 2024 film, still hosted on YouTube.
context: This is the Focus Features trailer on YouTube, published 30 September 2024. The uploader’s own title still mentions a 25 December theatrical date. That line belongs to the trailer as uploaded; it is not a BRYME showtimes listing. BRYME does not host the file and does not autoplay it.

The clip is on this page because Nosferatu is one of the five homepage heroes, and this title page is where those slides send you. BRYME lists a 2024 horror film directed by Robert Eggers, about 143 minutes, with Bill Skarsgård, Nicholas Hoult, Lily-Rose Depp, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Emma Corrin and Willem Dafoe in the billed cast. Country on this page is the United States; languages listed include English, Romanian and Russian.

A studio trailer is advertising. It is not the 1922 Murnau film, and it is not a plot guide. For BRYME’s catalogue notes and legal viewing pointers, read below the player. If YouTube withholds the embed, use the fallback link.

interstellar.name: Interstellar - Trailer - Official Warner Bros. UK
interstellar.description: Warner Bros. UK & Ireland YouTube trailer for Interstellar, published 16 May 2014.
interstellar.figcaption: The Warner Bros. UK & Ireland YouTube trailer for Christopher Nolan’s 2014 film. Play is on demand; no autoplay.
context: The player embeds a trailer uploaded by Warner Bros. UK & Ireland on 16 May 2014. That is the YouTube publish date shown on the watch page. BRYME does not host the video. The preview image is YouTube’s hqdefault thumbnail for this ID.

This title is BRYME’s rankings hero and sits on the popular and editor’s-pick lists, which is why the embed is worth keeping in good shape. The catalogue lists a 2014 science-fiction film directed by Christopher Nolan, about 169 minutes, in English, from the United Kingdom and the United States. The billed cast on this page includes Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, Bill Irwin, Ellen Burstyn and Michael Caine.

The trailer is the studio’s marketing cut from 2014. It is not BRYME’s ending explainer and not a physics lecture. Those, when they exist on BRYME, are separate articles linked from this page. Use Where to watch legally for licensed options. If the embed fails, open the same video on YouTube.

oppenheimer.name: Oppenheimer | New Trailer
oppenheimer.description: Universal Pictures’ YouTube trailer for Oppenheimer, published 8 May 2023.
oppenheimer.figcaption: Universal Pictures’ YouTube trailer for the 2023 film. Embedded from YouTube; BRYME does not host it.
context: This embed is Universal Pictures’ trailer on YouTube, published 8 May 2023. BRYME does not host or re-upload it. The player is poster-first: you see YouTube’s preview image until you press play. There is no autoplay on this title page.

The clip is here as the verified trailer for a flagship title page, not as a history documentary. BRYME lists a 2023 drama directed by Christopher Nolan, in English, from the United Kingdom and the United States. The billed cast on this page includes Cillian Murphy, Emily Blunt, Matt Damon, Robert Downey Jr., Florence Pugh and Josh Hartnett.

Do not take a trailer as a timeline of the Manhattan Project. Credits, runtime quirks in third-party databases, and streaming windows are easy to get wrong; this page only repeats facts already on the BRYME record. For licensed viewing, use Where to watch legally. If YouTube blocks the embed, use the fallback link under the frame.

dune-part-two.name: Dune Part Two | Official Trailer (2024)
dune-part-two.description: Trailer for Dune: Part Two uploaded on the AMC Theatres YouTube channel on 15 December 2023.
dune-part-two.figcaption: A trailer upload on the AMC Theatres YouTube channel for Denis Villeneuve’s second Dune film — not a BRYME-hosted file.
context: The video ID on this page is a trailer uploaded to the AMC Theatres YouTube channel on 15 December 2023. That is the channel YouTube names as the uploader. It is not a claim that AMC produced the film, and it is not Warner Bros.’ channel. BRYME does not host the file.

This title page is one of the flagship movie pages the Movies hub points to, which is why the embed is kept. BRYME lists a 2024 science-fiction film directed by Denis Villeneuve, about 166 minutes, in English, with Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, Josh Brolin, Austin Butler and Florence Pugh in the billed cast. Wikidata’s country list for the title is long; the page already treats that as a co-production rather than inventing a single origin.

The trailer is advertising for the sequel. It is not a recap of Part One and not a spoiler sheet. Read the notes below for BRYME’s catalogue text, and use Where to watch legally for licensed options. If the embed is unavailable, open the same YouTube URL from the fallback line.

This page is a flagship Movies-hub title, which is why the player is here. BRYME lists a 2019 Korean-language film from South Korea, directed by Bong Joon-ho, about 132 minutes, with Song Kang-ho, Lee Sun-kyun, Cho Yeo-jeong, Choi Woo-shik, Park So-dam and Jang Hye-jin in the billed cast.

A 2019 trailer is marketing. It is not a substitute for the film and not a BRYME review of awards. Awards chatter is easy to inflate; this block does not add it. Use the notes below for BRYME’s own text, and Where to watch legally for licensed options. If YouTube withholds the embed, use the fallback link.

spider-man-brand-new-day.figcaption: The Spider-Man YouTube channel’s official trailer, published 18 March 2026. BRYME does not host the file.
context: The player embeds the official trailer uploaded by the Spider-Man YouTube channel (@spiderman) on 18 March 2026. That is the watch-page uploader and date. It is not an IGN copy and not a fan edit. BRYME does not host the file. Sound starts only when you press play.

A trailer is marketing. It is not the film, not a recap, and not BRYME’s review. Credits on that upload name Destin Daniel Cretton as director and Tom Holland, Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Tramell Tillman, Michael Mando and Mark Ruffalo in the billed cast.
If YouTube blocks the embed, use the fallback link under the frame. Where to watch legally on this page is for licensed options — BRYME does not stream the movie.

If the embed fails, use the YouTube link. Digital/retail windows belong to Disney’s own timetable, not to a pirate site.
